name: BXP, Inc.
executive_summary: BXP is a large, gateway-market office REIT (Boston, New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Seattle, Washington DC) owning roughly 179 properties and 52.6 million net rentable square feet of primarily premier workplaces. The quantitative screen rates the name a buy, though the screen payload carries zero passed models and zero populated metrics, so the signal rests on an incomplete quantitative base. The value case hinges on durable operating cash flow (~$1.25bn in FY2025 per Yahoo fallback), an active asset-disposal programme targeting ~$1.9bn in net proceeds, and leasing momentum cited in recent earnings coverage. The central debate is whether premium assets and balance-sheet repair can offset structural office demand risk (hybrid work, AI-driven headcount pressure), rising interest burden, and recurring impairment charges ($85.8m on consolidated assets and $145.1m on the Gateway Commons joint venture in FY2025, per the FY2025 10-K body extract).
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, BXP offers exposure to irreplaceable urban office assets at a point where management is explicitly pivoting from growth-at-any-cost to capital discipline. At the September 2025 Investor Day (disclosed in the FY2025 10-K), management outlined a four-part plan: grow occupancy, complete selective development, execute dispositions targeting ~$1.9bn in net proceeds, and pursue private-equity partnerships on selected assets. FY2025 dispositions already generated ~$682.5m net proceeds on ~$702.6m gross sales (10-K), demonstrating execution capacity.

Operating fundamentals show modest top-line resilience: H1 2026 total revenue was $1.77bn versus $1.73bn in H1 2025 (Q2 2026 10-Q), and net income attributable to BXP for H1 2026 was $170.2m versus $150.2m prior year (Q2 2026 10-Q). Yahoo fallback shows FY2025 net income of $276.8m (diluted EPS $1.74) recovering sharply from FY2024’s $14.3m ($0.09), though both years are distorted by equity-method investee results and gain/loss on securities.

Cash economics are more stable than GAAP earnings: FY2025 operating and free cash flow were both ~$1.25bn (Yahoo fallback), with TTM operating/free cash flow of ~$1.28bn (`screening_snapshot.json`). Dividends paid were ~$643m in FY2025 (Yahoo), implying roughly 1.9x cash coverage — relevant for income-oriented value accounts.

The buy screen aligns with a “quality at a discount” framing: premier portfolio, visible deleveraging pathway, and improving leasing narrative (Morningstar, 16 Aug 2026: “Strong Leasing Drives Occupancy Improvement With Management Guiding to Higher Levels”). However, with `models_passed: 0`, `metrics_present: 0`, and `data_quality_score: 0.0` in the screening snapshot, the quantitative endorsement should be treated as directional rather than evidence-backed until verify-before-trade metrics are populated.
financial_review:
**Annual (10-K — primary filing, partial body extract)**

Two SEC 10-K body extracts are available: FY2024 (filed Feb 2025) and FY2025 (filed Feb 2026). Both are truncated at ~80,000 characters before Item 8 consolidated financial statements; annual income-statement and balance-sheet line items below therefore fall back to `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo), explicitly noted.

From the FY2025 10-K body (qualitative and selected disclosed amounts, not Yahoo):

- Portfolio: 179 commercial properties, ~52.6m net rentable sq ft; weighted-average remaining lease term ~7.9 years; ~5.6m sq ft of new leasing in 2025 with average term ~10.1 years.
- Dispositions: eight sales, ~$702.6m gross / ~$682.5m net proceeds; gains on sales ~$175.0m (BXP).
- Impairments: ~$85.8m on consolidated assets approved for sale; ~$145.1m “other than temporary” impairment on Gateway Commons joint venture.
- Development: eight projects under construction (~3.5m sq ft); estimated remaining spend ~$2.5bn of ~$3.9bn total pipeline investment.
- Capital markets (2025): repaid $850m of 3.20% senior notes; upsized commercial paper to $750m; extended $2.25bn revolver and $700m term loan to 2030; issued $1.0bn of 2.00% exchangeable senior notes due 2030 (also detailed in 8-K, 29 Sep 2025).

Revenue has grown modestly (+6% over two years), but leverage remains heavy: net debt of ~$15.1bn against common equity of ~$5.15bn (Yahoo, FY2025). Interest expense has risen ~13% from FY2023 to FY2025, consistent with the 10-K’s warning that maturing lower-coupon debt refinances into a higher-rate environment. Retained earnings are deeply negative (~–$1.67bn), reflecting cumulative distributions and historical charges.

**Gaps**

- 10-K body extracts do not include audited consolidated statements; full annual P&L, FFO reconciliation, and covenant metrics are unavailable in-body.

- Investegate/RNS entries in the index are entity mismatches and must not be used for BXP, Inc.
risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical / sector:** The FY2025 10-K identifies concentrated exposure to six gateway markets and warns that hybrid/remote work and AI-driven workforce reductions “could decrease overall demand for workplaces and negatively impact market rental rates and property values.” Tech, financial, and government-contractor tenant concentrations amplify cyclicality.

**Leverage / liquidity:** Total debt ~$17.4bn and net debt ~$15.1bn (Yahoo FY2025) against ~$5.2bn equity. Commercial paper outstanding ~$750m (Q2 2026 10-Q). The 10-K states: “Covenants in our debt agreements could adversely affect our financial condition” and “Our degree of leverage could limit our ability to obtain additional financing.” Refinancing risk is explicit: maturing debt bears lower coupons than current market rates. August 2026 news reports BPLP agreeing to sell $700m in notes to address ~$1bn due October 2026 (Stock Titan, 17 Aug 2026).

**Accounting / asset values:** FY2025 impairments of $85.8m (consolidated) and $145.1m (Gateway Commons JV) signal mark-down pressure. Q3 2025 included a large quarterly GAAP loss (Yahoo). No going-concern language was found in available filing extracts.

**Development execution:** ~$2.5bn of estimated remaining spend on eight active projects (10-K) in a challenged office demand environment creates capital allocation risk if dispositions slip.

**Governance / data quality:** The filings index contamination with Beximco Pharmaceuticals RNS announcements is a research-process red flag; verify all future filings by CIK 1037540, not ticker alone.

**Competitive:** 10-K notes competition from other premier workplace owners and from remote-work alternatives that reduce aggregate office demand.

RiskTags: cyclical, leverage, liquidity, accounting, competitive, other

research_rationale: Deep research partially confirms the screen’s buy bias via strong cash generation, visible disposition-led deleveraging, and leasing improvement, but heavy leverage, office-sector structural headwinds, impairment charges, and absent quantitative screen metrics warrant a measured rather than full-conviction overlay.
